orig_text:
o  if the certificate's signatureAlgorithm uses no hash functions or
      uses multiple hash functions, then this channel binding type's
      channel bindings are undefined at this time (updates to is channel
      binding type may occur to address this issue if it ever arises).
correct_text:
o  if no unique suitable hash function could be identified from the
      certificate's signatureAlgorithm, then use the identity function.
notes:
ML-DSA [FIPS-204] falls into the third category of the original text, as it
does not have associated hash, although it uses SHAKE128 & SHAKE256 internally
(there are probably other examples as well). This in turn leads to issues
around channel binding implementation like in [1], where it's not clear how to
create the needed digest.

The proposal is to close the gap in such a way that does not require any
knownedge of the connection internal state, thus simpy the identity function is
used for the digest.

An alternative of similar type would be to use a specified hash instead, e.g.
SHA-256. This would be a bit easier for final implementation, for example
PostgreSQL uses OpenSSL and all what's needed is to pass chosen algorithm to
X509_digest. OpenSSL does not have an "identity function" as an algorithm, so
the main proposed change would be a bit more verbose to implement, but it's
concidered to be conceptually simpler.

[1]: https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/CAFjYY+JCCQeh03nzVG6Rs9MUgU_kOvhMbNaaS6kn_c4CcAZkTg@mail.gmail.com
